label: ConfirmPayment

label: FillOrder

label: MarkOrderPending

label: RaiseInvoice

label: RegisterCustomer

label: OrderStaff

label: OrderStaff
rationale: OrderStaff is a real role explicitly referenced in the domain requirements, and the swimlane does not contradict any listed gold element.

label: Customer
rationale: A Customer swimlane for submitting orders is traceable to REQ-F-13, and it introduces no direct contradiction with the gold elements.

label: Accountant

label: BrowseProducts->SubmitOrder
rationale: The transition invents a “BrowseProducts” activity absent from the domain requirements, though it does not directly contradict the gold order-processing elements.

label: CloseOrder->RaiseInvoice
rationale: Closing an order requires it to be shipped with its invoice already paid, so a close-to-raise-invoice transition is unsupported and reverses the required invoice/payment-before-close flow.

label: ConfirmPayment->RejectPayment
rationale: A transition from confirming a payment to rejecting it is not required and contradicts the payment lifecycle, since only pending payments can be rejected while confirmed payments become completed.

label: FillOrder->RaiseInvoice
rationale: The transition corresponds to REQ-F-28 and REQ-F-31, which allow an invoice to be raised after an order is filled, and it does not contradict any gold element.

label: FillOrder->ShipOrder
rationale: The transition from filling an order to shipping it is directly supported by REQ-F-20 and REQ-F-25 and matches the gold transition Fill Order->Ship Order without contradiction.

label: MarkOrderPending->FillOrder
rationale: The transition reflects the allowed progression from setting an order to pending (REQ-F-18) to filling it while pending (REQ-F-20) and does not contradict any gold element.

label: RaiseInvoice->CloseOrder
rationale: Raising an invoice does not directly lead to closing an order; closing requires the order to be shipped and its invoice paid, matching the gold flow through payment and not a RaiseInvoice->CloseOrder transition.

label: RaiseInvoice->SubmitPayment
rationale: The transition corresponds to the domain sequence of raising an invoice and then submitting a payment against that issued invoice, matching the gold transition Send Invoice→Make Payment.

label: ReceiveOrder->MarkOrderPending
rationale: REQ-F-18 requires receiving a submitted order by setting its status to pending, and the transition does not contradict any listed gold element.

label: RegisterCustomer->BrowseProducts
rationale: The RegisterCustomer->BrowseProducts transition is an invented workflow not specified in the requirements, though it does not contradict any gold element.

label: SubmitOrder->ReceiveOrder
rationale: The transition reflects the domain flow from submitting an order (REQ-F-13) to receiving a submitted order (REQ-F-18), and it does not contradict the gold transition from Make an Order to Receive order.

label: SubmitPayment->ConfirmPayment
rationale: It reflects REQ-F-32/F-35/F-36, where a submitted payment is recorded as pending and can later be confirmed/completed, and it does not contradict the gold Make Payment -> Accept Payment flow.

label: +accountNumber: String
rationale: The account number corresponds to the domain's optional customer bank account and the referenced bank account numbers, and it does not contradict any gold element.

label: +paymentMethod: PaymentMethod
rationale: REQ-F-05 and REQ-F-48 require recording a restricted payment method on an order, and using paymentMethod rather than the gold model’s method name is a naming/presentation difference that does not contradict any gold element.

label: +paymentMethod: PaymentMethod
rationale: The attribute records the required payment method for a payment and uses the PaymentMethod type, without contradicting any gold element.

label: +imageUrl: String
rationale: imageUrl captures the required product image as a URL string and does not contradict the gold Product.image attribute.

label: BankAccount
rationale: BankAccount is traceable to REQ-F-02 and REQ-F-45 as the optional customer bank-account data, and separating it as a class does not contradict the gold model’s Customer.bankAccount attribute.

label: records >
rationale: The relationship captures REQ-F-12’s association of payments with exactly one invoice and invoices with any number of payments, and aligns with the gold R:Invoice--Payment relationship.

label: contains >
rationale: REQ-F-06 and REQ-F-07 require order items to belong to exactly one order and to exist only as part of that order, so an Order–OrderItem containment relationship is traceable and does not contradict the gold Order–OrderItem relationship.
